events.description: Saturday night confrontation between Deputy Special Officer Moore and federation Indians at fiesta; Indians challenged Moore's authority, threatened violence, federation police asserted sole authority
Mesa Grande Indian fiesta attended by approximately 200 Indians and 50 white people; described as peaceful by witnesses Prather, Booth, and Stough who left at 9 p.m.

Meeting held in old adobe building to discuss allowing Indian children to attend public school and close reservation school; Conradt attended and agreed to recommend Bureau assistance for enlarging public school
Moore sent wire to Commissioner Collier reporting alleged lawlessness at Mesa Grande fiesta and accusing Willis of inciting Indians
Moore received answering wire from Collier backing Moore's authority; read to assembled Indians at Mesa Grande
Quiet and orderly meeting where Moore read Collier's telegram; Indian police covered four ringleaders; federation Indians struck dumb by Collier's support of government authority
Historical shooting incident at Campo reservation involving officers who had attempted to make arrests; referenced by Moore as precedent

events.location: Sycuan Indian Reservation, San Diego County
events.description: Prather, Mrs. Prather, Mrs. Purl Willis and her daughter visited Sycuan reservation; Prather was stopped by Indian Frank Wachano claiming orders from Riverside not to allow Prather on reservation
Two Indians including Dan Ames came to Prather's home requesting he visit Sycuan reservation to discuss controversial matters

Meeting held under ramada at Captain Chaparosa's home; Anderson proposed volunteer survey of reservation lines; Indians agreed to accept offer; meeting lasted all afternoon with approximately 15-20 Indian men and women

Follow-up conference called by Anderson at Captain Chaparosa's home; Anderson arrived late; Indians expressed disappointment with Anderson's work; dispute over proposed land exchange near Hot Springs; Anderson promised maps and report within 10 days
Willis addressed letter to Nathan Margold, Solicitor of Interior Department, regarding Mesa Grande incident
E.J. Geehan of DOJ Bureau of Investigation investigated Willis's activities among Mission Indians; resulted in no charges being preferred against Willis
Geehan wrote to Willis confirming no charges were preferred as result of investigation; noted Willis had been invited to National Capital
Castillo, Albanes, Couro, and Willis sent letter to Senate Indian Affairs Committee contesting Moore's account of Mesa Grande incident
H. R. Prather wrote to Congressman Edgar Howard contesting Moore's telegram to Collier about Mesa Grande fiesta
Notary Ethlin Thurmond notarized Prather's letter and Mrs. Frank Booth's attestation
Statement by Castillo, Couro, and Willis certified facts about resurvey and exchange of land at Los Coyotes reservation
Senate Indian Affairs Committee special hearings on conditions of Indians; witnesses testified; committee invited additional written submissions
Chairman questioned Dady, Rieger, and La Chusa about armed Indians at Los Coyotes meeting; Rieger stated Nicholas Chaparosa had gun in plain view

events.type: attempt to get Indians to sign land exchange paper
events.description: Anderson visited reservation when people were working and tried to get Chutnicut to sign paper authorizing exchange of strip of Indian land near Hot Springs for land near Manuel Chaparosa's home; Chutnicut refused

events.location: Soboba Indian Reservation, near San Jacinto
events.description: Anderson claimed to have made extensive survey over 100 pages with maps of Soboba Reservation for Dady and Indians; given to spokesman Majado; showed Indian lines took in valuable ranch property

financial_transactions.description: Federation Indians claimed a badge like Moore's could be purchased for 15 cents, challenging the legitimacy of his authority
Willis stated to have provided services to Los Coyotes Indians voluntarily without charge over several years
Anderson offered to survey Los Coyotes reservation lines for free if Indians would assist with brush cutting, rather than accept Dady's commission

testimony.witness_title: Deputy Special Officer at Large, United States Indian Service
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Mesa Grande fiesta incident August 1933; confrontation with federation Indians; Willis and Prather inciting resistance
testimony.key_claims: Moore testified that federation Indians challenged his authority at Mesa Grande fiesta, threatened violence, claimed only federation police had authority, and that Willis had urged Indians to resist government officers. He claimed Indians were armed. He described de-escalating a potentially violent confrontation and sending telegram to Collier for backing. He characterized Willis, Prather, and Collett as dangerous racketeers interfering with government work.

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Mesa Grande incident; Los Coyotes resurvey; Mission Indian welfare
testimony.key_claims: Co-signed letters asserting Moore made false charges; Willis never advised resorting to violence; Federation police never carry arms or offered physical resistance; Anderson failed to properly retrace old survey lines; Indians were not incited by Willis or Castillo to sign away rights.

testimony.witness_title: Mission Indian advocate; Mission Indian Federation
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Mesa Grande incident; Los Coyotes resurvey; Indian Bureau conduct; Sycuan reservation espionage
testimony.key_claims: Moore made totally false charges manufactured out of whole cloth; no disturbance occurred while Willis was at fiesta on August 4, 1933; Willis left at 10:30 p.m. before alleged incidents; Willis's car was set on fire and Moore's police did nothing; Anderson attempted to fraudulently obtain Indian signature on land exchange paper; Dady and Anderson acted in concert against Indian interests; Indian policemen are cause of friction among Mission Indians; no Indian policemen are needed in southern California.

testimony.witness_title: Citizen, La Jolla; Mission Indian advocate
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.committee: Senate Indian Affairs Committee and House Indian Committee
testimony.subject: Mesa Grande fiesta account; Sycuan reservation gag rule and espionage; Moore's false accusations
testimony.key_claims: Prather and companions left Mesa Grande fiesta at 9 p.m. finding it entirely peaceful and orderly; school meeting was open and non-secret; Moore's telegram to Collier was maliciously conceived with neither truth nor basic fact; Frank Wachano attempted to prevent Prather from entering Sycuan reservation on orders from Riverside; Riverside office engaged in gag rule and espionage; Wachano was stool pigeon for superintendent.

testimony.witness_title: Local Superintendent, Mission Indian Agency, Riverside
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Armed Indians at Los Coyotes; Anderson survey commission
testimony.key_claims: Dady was not present at the Los Coyotes meeting but stated Rieger was there and would testify he saw Indians armed. Implied armed Indians were present.

testimony.witness_title: Chief of E.C.W., Mission Indian Agency under Dady
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Whether Indians were armed at Los Coyotes meeting
testimony.key_claims: Rieger stated he was not familiar with all men present but saw Nicholas Chaparosa had a gun in plain view that afternoon. Was uncertain about other men because he was not familiar with them at the time.

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Whether Nicholas Chaparosa had a gun at the meeting
testimony.key_claims: La Chusa knew Nicholas Chaparosa and saw him that afternoon but stated he was not even a federation police, implying he did not have a gun in an official capacity; testimony appeared to contest Rieger's claim.

testimony.committee: Senate Indian Affairs Committee (referenced in September 10, 1934 letter)
testimony.subject: Moore's accusations about armed Indians at Mesa Grande fiesta
testimony.key_claims: McGee stated that Moore's accusations against Indians carrying arms at Mesa Grande fiesta were false.
